summary: Iteration 3 (integrations, patient portal, cron reminders, embeddable widget) fully green. 15/15 backend pytest cases pass and all requested frontend flows (portal login → home → logout, IntegrationsPanel save with masked-secret round-trip, Developer widget-card & copy button) pass end-to-end. Providers stay unconfigured by default and notifications correctly log status='skipped_not_configured' — treated as PASS. Cron endpoint enforces bearer WEBHOOK_CRON_SECRET (401 without, 200 {status:accepted} with correct secret) and flips reminder_sent=true on tomorrow's appointments. Widget.js served with application/javascript. Regression on staff auth/login and dashboard stats confirmed.

issues: React console warning: duplicate keys `/public/patients` and `/public/appointments` — endpoints array probably uses `path` as the key while multiple rows share the same path (GET/POST or GET/PUT). Change key to `${method}-${path}` to remove the warning.

action_items: (Nice-to-have) Fix duplicate React key warning on Developer endpoints list by combining method+path as the key.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py has grown to 855 lines. Split into modules: integrations.py (providers/notify), portal.py, cron.py, widget.py — reduces risk and speeds tests.
notify() and _run_appointment_reminders() couple email+whatsapp channels; consider per-event channel targeting (e.g., reminders WhatsApp-only) as future config.

_run_appointment_reminders runs in-process via asyncio.create_task without persistence — if the pod restarts mid-run, partially-processed appts won't be retried until next day. Consider a lightweight job table or making the endpoint idempotent-and-batched.

portal/appointments|prescriptions|invoices match patient by NAME (a.get('patient')==pt.name). If two patients share the same name in a tenant, they will see each other's records. Match on patient_id (link at creation) to eliminate this cross-record risk.

PortalLogin.jsx sets loading=true but never resets it on the success path (relies on navigate); acceptable but if navigate is blocked (e.g., portal token invalid) the button stays disabled — set loading=false in finally.
CORSMiddleware still uses allow_origin_regex='.*' with allow_credentials=True — accept for header-based auth but flag for security review before production.
widget.js is served unauthenticated (correct) but has no cache headers; adding Cache-Control: public, max-age=300 would reduce backend hits.
